items.answer: 2024 One acknowledges that both Valli and Mandela exhibit aspirations, yet their expressions of desire and vision differ significantly. Valli, in “Madam Rides the Bus,” harbors a personal desire to experience the thrill of riding a bus, symbolic of freedom and exploration in her confined world. Their journeys highlight the distinction between individual desires and collective visions in shaping personal and societal destinies.

These pieces are from the stories, Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom and The Trees. In both the pieces, resilience of the human spirit has proved to be able to eliminate discrimination. In Nelson Mandela, Mandela had a grit and determination to abolish the racism that prevailed against the blacks in South Africa. He fought that discrimination while facing a lot of challenges in his life only because he was resilient. Similarly, in the poem ‘The Trees’, the poet uses the image of trees to depict the journey of women in the world to fight for their rights. She had shown how hard work, perseverance and grit can defeat any challenge in the way to attain our human rights. To conclude, I’d like to say that we should learn from these pieces that no matter what comes in our way, we should have resilience of the spirit to transcend discrimination and speak up for our rights. Thank you
